sents.t: In November, I started volunteering on Tuesday evenings at the Oakville Library, which offers a free citizenship class.
The students are immigrants who have had green cards for at least five years and are preparing for the citizenship test.
The teacher, Mr. Okafor, came from Nigeria thirty years ago.
He’s the kind of teacher who makes everyone feel welcome.
I help students who need extra practice.
My favorite student is Doña Carmen, Ana’s grandmother, the woman who taught me to dance at the wedding.
She’s seventy-eight, and she has lived in America for forty years.
“I always wanted to become a citizen,” she told me, “but I was afraid of the test.”
In the civics part, students answer questions about American history and government, like “Who was the first president?” Students also have to read and write in English.
We practiced with flashcards every week, and she learned the hundred questions faster than anyone.
On test day, her family waited outside.
When she came out, she was holding a paper and smiling.
Next month, she will take the oath at a ceremony where hundreds of new citizens are welcomed.
